canonical.name: Finite authenticated protocol interface
canonical.detail: Defines finite key and transcript alphabets, ideal authenticated public communication, finite quantum registers, party outputs, and the normalized cq output state for each adversarial strategy.

canonical.name: Finite classical key-copy channel
canonical.detail: Explicit finite Kraus operators copy only a dephased classical key register; complete positivity and trace preservation are proved locally.

canonical.name: Trace norm of classical block operators
canonical.detail: Finite spectral proof that the trace norm of a block-diagonal operator is the sum of the trace norms of its self-adjoint blocks.

canonical.name: Abort-aware real and ideal security errors
canonical.detail: Keeps the real abort branch, transcript, and adversary marginal; uses unconditional abort-weighted secrecy and correctness errors.

canonical.name: Correctness error as copy-replacement distance
canonical.detail: A direct block calculation shows that replacing Bob's key by a copy of Alice's changes the normalized cq state by exactly the mismatch probability.

canonical.name: Well-defined abort-aware ideal state
canonical.detail: Checks conditional marginals and the ideal output directly from finite classical block sums, including the zero-acceptance case.

canonical.name: Composable sum-of-errors theorem
canonical.detail: Local triangle-inequality proof after copying Alice's key; block trace-norm equality identifies the secrecy term and the correctness lemma identifies the mismatch term.

sources.title: Christopher Portmann and Renato Renner, Cryptographic Security of Quantum Key Distribution (2014), full arXiv text
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete author-hosted arXiv PDF. Relevant full-text sections were extracted and inspected locally; the source supplies the ideal-real QKD model, unconditional abort-weighted correctness and secrecy definitions, and Theorem 4.1 proof route.
sources.locator: §§3.1–3.3; §§4.1–4.3, especially Eqs. (12)–(15), footnote 19, and Theorem 4.1 proof.
sources.read_locator: Extracted the complete 58-page PDF and inspected §§3.1–3.3, §§4.1–4.3 through the full copy-key/triangle proof of Theorem 4.1, including the unconditional correctness convention and the acceptance multiplier in secrecy.
sources.extent: One of two independent research-paper treatments of the ideal-real criterion and separate correctness/secrecy theorem. The library proof supplies each finite-dimensional calculation locally.
sources.support: Primary detailed treatment of authenticated public transcripts, abort-preserving ideal key resources, epsilon_cor and epsilon_sec with the acceptance factor, and the copy-A-into-B triangle-inequality proof. Its adversary side-information register includes the public transcript; the local development names transcript T explicitly.

contents.name: Finite QKD protocol and authenticated public transcript
contents.detail: §§3.1–3.2 define the two-party protocol interface and explain that the authentic channel delivers messages faithfully while disclosing them to Eve.

contents.name: Abort-aware ideal key and accepted conditional state
contents.detail: §4.2, Eqs. (12)–(13), keeps the abort probability and conditions the accepted state before multiplying by 1-p_abort.

contents.name: Correctness, secrecy, and their sum bound
contents.detail: §4.3, Eqs. (14)–(15), footnote 19, Theorem 4.1, and its copy-key/triangle proof.

contents.name: Trace norm convention
contents.detail: §4.1 reduces the resource distinguisher criterion to trace distance; the local criterion uses the published half-trace-norm state convention.

contents.name: Abort-weighted finite examples
contents.detail: §4.3 supplies the acceptance-weighted convention used by the explicit one-bit calculation.

contents.name: Secrecy/correctness distinction
contents.detail: §4.3 defines the two errors separately; the example constructs explicit extremal finite output states.

sources.title: Joseph M. Renes, Quantum Information Theory, ETH Zürich lecture notes (HS2014; revised 4 February 2015), full lecture notes
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete author-hosted graduate quantum-information lecture-note PDF. The complete §8.3 QKD security proposition and proof were extracted and inspected locally; §2.1 in this version treats fidelity rather than trace distance.
sources.locator: §8.3, Quantum cryptography, Eqs. (8.6)–(8.10) and Proposition 8.3.1 with proof.
sources.read_locator: Extracted the complete 187-page lecture notes and inspected the entire §8.3 passage through the complete proof of Proposition 8.3.1, including the accepted-state normalization, abort weighting, copy-key hybrid, and triangle inequality.
sources.extent: Full lecture-note treatment of the QKD correctness/secrecy-to-composable-security theorem; an additional complete exposition alongside the two separate research-paper teams.
sources.support: States the abort-weighted secrecy and unconditional correctness conventions and proves their additive implication. The local items supply the finite block trace-norm calculation explicitly.

contents.name: Correctness, secrecy, and QKD composability
contents.detail: §8.3 gives the output alphabet K union bottom, abort probability, normalized accepted state, and epsilon_sec=(1-p_abort)D(...).

contents.name: Additive composable security theorem
contents.detail: Proposition 8.3.1 and its full proof state and prove epsilon=epsilon_cor+epsilon_sec.

contents.name: Finite abort-weighted example
contents.detail: §8.3 provides the exact accepted-state weighting convention used in the calculation.

contents.name: Secrecy and correctness as separate criteria
contents.detail: §8.3 states separate conditions; the example gives explicit states where either one vanishes while the other does not.

sources.title: M. Ben-Or, M. Horodecki, D. W. Leung, D. Mayers, and J. Oppenheim, The Universal Composable Security of Quantum Key Distribution (2005), full arXiv text
sources.source_kind_detail: Complete author-hosted 20-page arXiv PDF. The finite-dimensional model, authentication assumptions, variable-length abort convention, and ideal-real distinguishability derivation were extracted and inspected locally.
sources.read_locator: Extracted the complete PDF and inspected §2 and the full §§4.1–4.3 derivation: finite-dimensional systems, ideal authentication and initial key, m=0 abort, simulator-preserved Eve view, ideal shared key, trace-distance distinguishing bound, and decomposition into equality/uniformity and privacy components.
sources.extent: Independent research-paper treatment by a separate author team of the ideal-real QKD criterion and universal-composition motivation; a second independent research source alongside Portmann–Renner. It does not present the same epsilon_cor+epsilon_sec theorem, which is independently proved locally from the two theorem treatments that do.
sources.support: Cross-checks the ideal authenticated-channel assumption, an abort-aware ideal shared key that preserves Eve's simulated view, and trace-distance comparison of real and ideal outputs. Its variable-length key model and initial authentication key are broader/different interface details; the local page states its finite fixed-key/common-abort convention explicitly.

contents.name: Finite quantum model and authentication assumptions
contents.detail: §2 states finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces, authenticated communication, and the initial authentication-key assumption.

contents.name: Ideal-real criterion and abort-preserving simulator
contents.detail: §§4.1–4.3 model m=0 as abort, preserve the real transcript/Eve view through the simulator, and compare final states by trace distance.

sources.read_locator: Extracted the complete 598-page textbook and inspected Chapter 1 §1.1.3, Eq. (1.181), and Chapter 2 §§2.2.1–2.2.2 through the finite Kraus and channel characterization passages.
sources.extent: Full textbook treatment supporting the finite-dimensional operator facts used by the A-page proofs.
sources.support: Independent book source for trace norms, singular-value spectral formulas, Kraus maps, and quantum channels; it does not replace any local proof.

contents.name: Trace norm finite spectral formula
contents.detail: Chapter 1, §1.1.3 gives the trace norm and singular-value characterization used in the local spectral proof.

contents.name: Finite Kraus maps and channels
contents.detail: Chapter 2, §2.2.2 treats Kraus representations and the completely-positive trace-preserving channel definition.

contents.name: Trace-distance norm convention
contents.detail: Watrous notes that the unhalved trace norm of a state difference is often called trace distance; the local item follows the library's published convention D=1/2||rho-sigma||_1.

canonical.name: Abort-weighted one-bit protocol calculation
canonical.detail: Computes the real and ideal output states, the exact trace distance 3/8, the zero correctness error, and the acceptance-weighted secrecy error.

canonical.name: Independent correctness and secrecy requirements
canonical.detail: Computes one state with perfect secrecy and maximal correctness error and a second with perfect correctness and nonzero secrecy error.
